projects.tagline: Retro arcade cabinet where you race reinforcement-learning policies on 8x8 Minesweeper
projects.short_description: An in-browser retro arcade cabinet running ONNX-exported reinforcement-learning policies on a deterministic 8x8 Minesweeper engine. Play a seeded board, watch the AI reason with a live action mask and confidence heatmap, race a checkpoint on the same seed, or run the whole nine-model library in CONCURRENT mode.
projects.long_description: Minesweeper RL Arcade is an in-browser retro arcade cabinet built around a deterministic 8x8 Minesweeper engine and a library of ONNX-exported reinforcement-learning policies. It has five modes: PLAY, where you clear a seeded board with a guaranteed-safe first click; AI, where a selected checkpoint plays the same seed with live confidence, per-cell distributions, and a legal-action mask; RACE, a side-by-side human-vs-policy comparison on an identical seed; CONCURRENT, where every checkpoint in the library steps through one board in lockstep with a CLEARED/DETONATED/STUCK scoreboard and points-sorted leaderboard; and MODELS, a details panel for each manifest checkpoint (family, method, architecture, training recipe, file size, and fixed-seed evaluation). The v2 library ships nine documented checkpoints across four families — a uniform baseline, solver-imitation behaviour clones, REINFORCE policy-gradient models, and kernel/single-conv ablations — evaluated from 0% to 61.4% win rate. The app is a static ES-module bundle that fetches models/manifest.json and runs inference through the pinned onnxruntime-web CDN; the engine, featurization, and action-mask contract stay frozen so scores remain comparable across checkpoints. It deploys to GitHub Pages from main at mines.livive.net, guarded by a smoke workflow that asserts the app, the manifest, and every model file are served live.

projects.tagline: Zero-backend, fully client-side browser RAG with local embeddings and WebGPU LLMs
projects.short_description: A 100% client-side Retrieval-Augmented Generation proof-of-concept that parses PDFs, chunks text, generates ONNX embeddings, builds an in-memory vector index, and runs local WebGPU language models entirely in the browser with no backend or external APIs.
projects.long_description: Northstar RAG POC is a static single-page application demonstrating retrieval-augmented generation entirely inside the browser with zero backend and zero external API calls. It extracts per-page text from PDFs using PDF.js, splits documents with a sliding-window chunker, generates embeddings via Transformers.js ONNX models, and stores 367 chunk vectors as contiguous Float32Array buffers in JavaScript heap memory for linear dot-product similarity search. Answers are generated by WebLLM with WebGPU acceleration, hot-swapping between Llama-3.2-1B, SmolLM2-1.7B, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B, or by four ONNX embedding models. When WebGPU is unavailable it falls back to a semantic retrieval view showing ranked matches and cosine scores. The demo is preloaded with 21 fictional Northstar Urgent Care Cooperative operational policy PDFs (64 pages) plus a 15-query evaluation benchmark including guardrail abstention cases. Built-in developer tools include a canvas PDF viewer, chunk visualizer, vector math inspector, raw prompt preview, and hardware diagnostics. It is hosted on GitHub Pages as a fully static bundle.

projects.tagline: Compiling bounded AI reasoning into static, deterministic instruction sets
projects.short_description: Compiled Domain Expertise (CDE) is an architectural specification that compiles bounded AI reasoning into a static, language-agnostic Domain Instruction Set, replacing runtime neural nets with a deterministic, sub-megabyte relational graph.
projects.long_description: CDE proposes severing knowledge acquisition from knowledge execution. At build time, high-capacity models operate offline as an empirical knowledge compiler (Empirical Knowledge Compilation, EKC) to explore a closed domain, extract candidate reasoning structures, and surface inferential dependencies. At runtime, only surviving validated structures execute after being lowered into a Domain Instruction Set (DIS). The Quantized Semantic Bottleneck Architecture (QSBA) uses an hourglass topology that decouples continuous, high-dimensional linguistic transducers from a discrete, integer-only core, targeting exact attribution, loud syntax checks, and microsecond execution on standard CPUs within a sub-megabyte budget. The repo includes the specification, a CCPA reference instance (QSBC), an algebra domain with an ingest/review workbench (FastAPI backend + React frontend), supporting dialogues, docs, and generated slide decks.
projects.notes: Dossier live probe list is empty; GitHub Pages disabled and homepage null, so no live demo. Primary artifact is an architectural specification (README) plus an algebra EKC workbench with a FastAPI/SQLAlchemy backend and React/Vite/Tailwind frontend. projects.tagline: Interpretable sentence classification via a semantic proposition bottleneck
projects.short_description: Infrastructure and experiments for QSBC, an interpretable sentence-classification architecture that inserts a human-meaningful semantic proposition bottleneck between input text and linear-probe prediction, applied to the CPRA subset of the C3PA privacy-policy dataset.
projects.long_description: QSBC replaces the direct text-to-label mapping of an uninterpretable transformer with a two-stage path: concept extraction, then a strictly linear probe, so concept attribution to class logits is analytically exact. This repo builds the data layer and experiments: a Dockerized PostgreSQL corpus of the parsed C3PA privacy policies matching the reference split, a chain-of-thought `cot` agent that generates atomic generalized rationales per sentence-label pair, the Phase 2 thoughts/ideas alphabet (statements clustered into canonical concepts), a FastAPI + Bootstrap SPA explorer, and Colab experiment notebooks (exp1-4) benchmarking the pipeline with a linear-probe ceiling reported at +9.8pt.

Physics uses a polytropic pressure-volume relation (P = P0 (V0 / V)^k, default isothermal k = 1) and an orifice flow approximation (Q = Cd A sqrt(2 dP / rho)) accounting for hydrostatic head, with water conserved as transferred volumes. The animated side view draws the apparatus, liquid flow, airflow, and a horizontal particle jet, with live readouts of elapsed time, jet velocity, flow rate, vessel volumes, and fill percentages. Controls include Invert (exchanging chamber elevations and reversing flow), Auto Invert with selectable triggers (jet speed, flow rate, chamber fill, elapsed cycle time, or settled condition) plus threshold and dwell, simulation Speed of 1x-16x, and Reset. It is a deliberate lumped approximation that omits turbulence, surface tension, viscosity, temperature change, and detailed inversion mechanics. No build step or external dependency is required; serve the directory as static files.

projects.tagline: Compiling bounded AI reasoning into static, deterministic instruction sets
projects.short_description: Compiled Domain Expertise (CDE) is an architectural specification that compiles bounded AI reasoning into a static, language-agnostic Domain Instruction Set, replacing runtime neural nets with a deterministic, sub-megabyte relational graph.
projects.long_description: CDE proposes severing knowledge acquisition from knowledge execution. At build time, high-capacity models operate offline as an empirical knowledge compiler (Empirical Knowledge Compilation, EKC) to explore a closed domain, extract candidate reasoning structures, and surface inferential dependencies. At runtime, only surviving validated structures execute after being lowered into a Domain Instruction Set (DIS). The Quantized Semantic Bottleneck Architecture (QSBA) uses an hourglass topology that decouples continuous, high-dimensional linguistic transducers from a discrete, integer-only core, targeting exact attribution, loud syntax checks, and microsecond execution on standard CPUs within a sub-megabyte budget. The repo includes the specification, a CCPA reference instance (QSBC), an algebra domain with an ingest/review workbench (FastAPI backend + React frontend), supporting dialogues, docs, and generated slide decks.

It is a deliberate lumped approximation that omits turbulence, surface tension, viscosity, temperature change, and detailed inversion mechanics. No build step or external dependency is required; serve the directory as static files.
